summary: Iteration 11 tested end-to-end. Backend: 13/13 new tests pass (test_iter11.py). Verified new seed (71 persons / 72 details / 15 lines), SK300 frame renders 4 sub-details totaling 6 required, GX300 frame 2 details totaling 2, /adjust with required=N sets per-detail required_overrides and persists, /mark-absent removes person from all cells + adds to absent list + increments shortage by 1 without autofill replacement, POST /log stores logged_at, GET /reports/absenteeism returns valid xlsx (only_logged=true filter works), and no regression on auto-plan/fill-shortages/suggest-lines. minor.issue: replace_one() wipes logged_at when regenerating; any manual adjust/mark-absent/fill-shortages after a schedule is logged silently clears logged_at because they all call generate_schedule which upserts a fresh doc without preserving logged_at. Consider preserving logged_at across regeneration (or documenting that any edit unlogs).

action_items: Consider preserving `logged_at` on POST /api/schedule / /adjust / /mark-absent / /fill-shortages regenerations — currently replace_one overwrites the whole doc and drops the timestamp. If unlog-on-edit is intentional, document it.

Existing /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (iter 6-10 suite) still asserts persons==76 and other counts based on the OLD seed and will now fail. Main agent should either delete or update that legacy suite to match the new 71-person seed to keep the regression bar green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py POST /schedule/{date}/log uses update_one with $set — safe. But every other write path uses generate_schedule → replace_one which strips logged_at silently. Bug or feature? Please clarify.
Cell key composition uses '||' as separator (row_name||line_key||detail). Any of those fields containing '||' would collide. Consider a safer join.
_generate_assignments fallback from cell_key_detail → cell_key_agg for required_overrides works correctly and matches the review spec.
